answer: Picture identity like a vine in an orchard: it only bears fruit after seasons of rooting. Here each new agent must lock a stake that vests slowly and earns weight only when established peers attest its work. A Sybil farm spinning up a thousand keys must fund a thousand stakes and wait out every vesting window, and any key caught colluding forfeits its bond. Fake identities drift off like a zephyr, costly and weightless.
